_purpose: Academic governance. What may change, who may change it, and what happens to certificates already issued when it does.
_principle: A certificate states what was demonstrated under a stated curriculum version. Changing the curriculum must never silently revalue a credential already awarded.

triggers: the competency graph changes - a node added, removed, or an edge redirected
a certification submission requirement is added or removed
major.effect_on_issued_certificates: none - issued certificates keep the version they were assessed under and remain valid. They are never retroactively upgraded or downgraded.

triggers: a capability or proof task is added
a unit's source document is corrected
wording is clarified with no change in what is assessed

curriculum_owner_approval.note: Single-holder governance is recorded honestly rather than dressed as a committee. When a second reviewer exists, this becomes two roles.

unit_retirement._rule: A unit is retired, never deleted - a student who certified against it must still be able to read what they were assessed on.
triggers: the source incident is superseded by a different root cause
the technology the incident depends on no longer exists
the fix is no longer correct
unit_retirement.deprecated_behaviour: still readable, no longer counts toward new certification
unit_retirement.retired_behaviour: readable and marked; historical certificates keep their reference

integrity_rules: No unit may exist without a source document in the corpus.
No competency may be certified without a portfolio submission.
No certificate may be issued without the curriculum version recorded on it.
A retired unit never invalidates a certificate already issued.
Research contributions by students are governed by RESEARCH_STANDARD.md, not by this file.

approval_log.summary: Initial curriculum: 6 competencies, 11 capabilities, portfolio certification, 4-requirement graduation.
